title: Incorrect error‑ignoring logic when should_ignore_error is None
detail: The new condition clears the error whenever `should_ignore_error` is unset, which removes normal exception handling. The original logic only cleared the error if the method existed and returned True.
note: Says the error is cleared whenever the hook is unset, which the planted `not` does.

title: Incorrect dunder method check in ChainableUndefined
detail: The condition incorrectly checks that the name does not start with double underscores while ending with them, causing AttributeError to be raised for valid dunder methods and not for invalid ones. This breaks Python protocol probing such as copy.copy and pickle.
note: Says the check of a name not starting with `__` raises for the wrong names, which the planted `!=` does.

title: TypeError due to comparing None with int
detail: The condition compares `max_digits <= decimal_places` when `max_digits` is None, causing a TypeError at runtime when this branch is evaluated.
note: Names the comparison of a None `max_digits` with `<=`.

title: Incorrect handling of __Host- cookie name prefix
detail: The function _has_valid_name_prefix incorrectly rejects all cookies with the "__Host-" prefix because it returns False when name.startswith("__host-") is True. It also incorrectly checks that the domain is NOT specified, whereas the __Host- prefix requires a specified domain. This causes valid __Host- cookies to be dropped.
note: Says `__Host-` cookies are always rejected, which the planted `and` does; its claim about the domain is wrong.

title: Incorrect boundary check for ZWJ at string end
detail: The condition `index <= (codepoint_count - 1)` incorrectly allows a ZWJ at the last code point to consume two positions, which is out of bounds and can lead to incorrect span calculations or an infinite loop. The correct check should be `index < (codepoint_count - 1)` or simply `index < codepoint_count` with a separate handling for the last code point.
note: Describes the planted `<=`: a ZWJ on the last code point steps the index past the end.
